subject: Dressing-room storage that feels calm
hook: We count your shoes before we draw a single shelf.
ig:
We count your shoes before we draw a single shelf. That's where a calm dressing room really starts.

Before any design, we ask what you actually own. Roughly how many pairs of shoes? How much long hanging versus shirts? Do you fold or hang knitwear? Handbags on shelves or in drawers?

Those answers decide the layout:
— how many drawers, and how deep
— where the long-hanging section goes
— whether shoes get pull-outs or angled shelves
— how much spare space to leave

Then we measure the room, show you the design in 3D, cut and build it in our Hanley workshop, check it before it leaves and fit it ourselves.

Planning fitted wardrobes or a dressing room? Comment CALM and we'll send you the link to book a free design consultation.
fb:
Here's something that surprises people at our design consultations: one of the first things we ask is how many pairs of shoes you've got.

It sounds odd, but a dressing room only stays calm if it's sized to what you own. Count first, then measure the room, then design — not the other way round.

This reel shows how we work from that first conversation to the finished fit: design in 3D, cut and built in our own workshop in Hanley, checked before it leaves, fitted by our own team.

If you're planning fitted wardrobes or a walk-in, book a free, no-obligation chat below.
